pr_title: net: dns_sd, mdns: support service type enumeration
pr_body:
Support DNS-SD Service Type Enumeration in the dns library and mdns_responder sample application.
    
For more information, please see Section 9, "Service Type Enumeration" in RFC 6763.
    
https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6763#section-9

Fixes #38673
pr_comments: The compliance failure is a false positive (bug in `./scripts/checkpatch.pl`). @galak, you may need to merge this one manually after it's approved.

So service type enumeration is working now. However, I do need to do a `avahi-browse -r -t -a` in order for avahi to send out the enumeration query. `avahi-discover` *does* send out the query but it seems that 'non-standard' services are not listed. I was able to test with `BOARD=stm32f746g_disco` and the macOS application `discovery` and `_zephyr._tcp.local` is indeed automatically discovered with this fix. The query / response highlighted: Details on the response packet: [Discovery](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/discovery-dns-sd-browser/id1381004916?mt=12) Just Works™: N.B: yes, I am also slightly terrified about the number of services that are advertising themselves on my network.

Also, note, that there is an enhancement ticket to provide an overall improvement of DNS-SD in v3.0.0, with emphasis on features such as this (service type enumeration), domain enumeration, as well as complete name, subtype, and non-local domain support.

For more information, see #38846
@rlubos , @jukkar - please have a look when you have a few minutes. The compliance failure is a false positive.
@galak / @nashif - either of you want to ack? Compliance failure is a false positive, so this needs to bee merged manually.
Added workaround for bug in compliance checks.

> ...
> However this message does not contain for instance my TXT record. If I compare to other devices that have MDNS support using wireshark, it seems like another device sends multiple messages:

The enumeration does not automatically respond with TXT records (service instances), just service types. A separate query is required for TXT records.

I have only been able to test with avahi in a Linux VM and the discovery app listed above, but I will try and test with `dns-sd` in the future as well. Are you using that on macOS?

If you would like to create a PR that solves your issue, I would be happy to review.
The `.` at the beginning of the query should be omitted.

issue_context.title: DNS-SD library does not support `_services._dns-sd._udp.local` meta-query for service enumeration
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
When building and running the mdns_responder sample, the device won't show up in avahi-browse or zeroconfServiceBrowser automatically. The device will only reply when you specifically query the following: `avahi-browse -t -r _zephyr._tcp`.

It seems like `_services._dns-sd._udp.<domain>` meta-query handling is not implemented.

When I open up zeroconfServiceBrowser or avahi-browse, the following is printed out at regular intervals: 
`net_dns_sd.dns_sd_extract_service_proto_domain: (rx_q[0]): could not get proto for '▒▒...'`

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The device should respond properly to the meta-query `_services._dns-sd._udp.<domain>` so that my device is displayed automatically in avahi-browse without having to specifically query `avahi-browse -t -r _zephyr._tcp`
comments:
The specific feature is called "service type enumeration" and is mentioned in the RFC on section 9.

https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6763#section-9

review_comments:
currently we are returning the `three-label <Instance>.<Service> name` rather than the `two-label <Service> name`.

So `zephyr._zephyr._tcp.local` rather than just `_zephyr._tcp.local`.

Inside of `dns_sd_handle_ptr_query()`, we call `add_ptr_record()` and that is hard-coded to add the instance rather than just the service.

Will likely also need to add `dns_sd_handle_service_query()` and something like `add_service_ptr_record()`.
should be fixed in latest revision. Will test with `avahi-discover` shortly.
We are checking int and size_t here, this could cause issues if value of N is very large. Better to add a cast `(int)N` here to in order to avoid some Coverity issue later.
These numbers come from the query for `_services._dns-sd._udp.local`
Perhaps `EADDRINUSE` here or `EADDRNOTAVAIL`
This matches what is done for PTR handling, so if it were changed here it would need to be changed there as well. I would prefer to address this in the larger rework task for v3
No need to break the string I guess? It should still fit within the limit.
The `ntohs()` looks unnecessary as the value is 0, so you can replace it by literal `0` value
This matches what is done for PTR handling, so if it were changed here it would need to be changed there as well. I would prefer to address this in the larger rework task for v3
ditto

Shouldn't we set this to 0 here?
Also wondering whether the `dns_sd_empty_txt` is cleared somewhere in the code.
It's set to zero as part of bss (uninitialized global variables, part of C std)
Hmm, I seem to have missed the memo that bss is initialized to zero in zephyr (as the name says it contains uninitialized vars thus was expecting `=0` here).
bss is set to zero as part of the C standard (C89). Zephyr follows suit ;-)
same here, please use `(int)N`
This value looks slightly weird, wouldn't `EINVAL` be more appropriate here or if we want to have network specific value, then perhaps `EADDRNOTAVAIL` could be used here
This matches what is done for PTR handling, so if it were changed here it would need to be changed there as well. I would prefer to address this in the larger rework task for v3

Perhaps this has been discussed earlier already, but just wondering why do we need to expose these extern variables in a public header file. Better would be to place any internal stuff to a private header file that could be placed to dns directory directly.

All dns_sd_rec are placed in an iterable struct section which requires a `uint16_t*` to facilitate ephemeral ports. It cannot be NULL atm. Rather than having several global `uint16_t` floating around solely for this purpose, I thought it best to make 1.

> Rather than having several global `uint16_t` floating around solely for this purpose, I thought it best to make 1.

Sure, but my question was that do we need to have these global symbols exposed in public header file, could these be placed in dns-sd private header file instead.

> > Rather than having several global `uint16_t` floating around solely for this purpose, I thought it best to make 1.
> 
> Sure, but my question was that do we need to have these global symbols exposed in public header file, could these be placed in dns-sd private header file instead.

They need to be in a public header so that API consumers can use `DNS_SD_REGISTER_SERVICE()`, `DNS_SD_REGISTER_TCP_SERVICE()`, `DNS_SD_REGISTER_UDP_SERVICE()`, etc.
Ok, no worries, sorry for the noise.
